name: How much contingency should I budget for a kitchen renovation?

mainEntity.name: How much contingency should I budget for a kitchen renovation?
mainEntity.text: How much contingency should I budget for a kitchen renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: A kitchen renovation should include a contingency because hidden issues are common once demolition begins. A typical reserve is 10% to 20% of the project budget, with older homes or complex luxury remodels often needing the higher end of that range. Contingency is used for surprises such as damaged subflooring, outdated wiring, plumbing corrections, wall issues, or code-related upgrades. It can also absorb small design changes or price differences when selected materials are unavailable. The key is not to treat contingency as extra spending money, but as protection against disruption and delays. Homeowners should keep it separate from the base construction budget and only use it when needed. In a market like Los Angeles, where older homes and custom designs are common, contingency planning is one of the best ways to keep the project on track when real-world conditions differ from the plan.
